artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled on a matter involving Metropolitan New York Presbytery's handling of a session that permitted a woman to expound Scripture during worship and held services without sermons. The SJC remitted the matter to the Presbytery to complete its work and report to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, while critiquing the procedural manner in which the matter was referred to the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: Rocky Mountain Presbytery sustained a candidate's ordination exam who held the view that women could teach (but not preach or exercise authority) in church ministries under the authority of the church session. TE James Urish complained that Presbytery erred in sustaining the candidate's exam. The SJC affirmed Presbytery's decision, finding no clear error, as neither the Westminster Standards nor the BCO explicitly address this specific application of 1 Timothy 2:12.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Robert Hopper challenged James River Presbytery's restriction on teaching and preaching about present-day prophecy and tongues. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that presbytery may limit such teaching for the welfare of the church when it determines the views threaten the church's peace or purity, while declining to issue a comprehensive doctrinal ruling.
